country_overview: France operates within the fully liberalised Eurozone foreign-exchange regime. There are no general exchange controls. The framework is governed by the European Central Bank (ECB), Banque de France, and French Customs (Douane).

summary.traveler: Travelers may bring in or take out unlimited amounts of euros and foreign currency. Cash movements of €10,000 or more (or equivalent) must be declared to French Customs.
summary.business: Businesses and individuals enjoy full freedom to hold, transfer, convert and repatriate foreign currency through authorised banks and financial institutions.

rules.bring_foreign_currency_in: Unlimited amounts of euros and foreign currency may be brought into France. Cash movements of €10,000 or more (or equivalent) must be declared to French Customs.
rules.take_foreign_currency_out: Unlimited amounts of euros and foreign currency may be taken out of France. Cash movements of €10,000 or more (or equivalent) must be declared to French Customs.
rules.cash_declaration_threshold: €10,000 or more (or equivalent in foreign currency or bearer negotiable instruments) at entry and exit. Declaration must be made to French Customs.
rules.resident_holding_rules: French residents may hold and maintain foreign currency accounts freely with authorised banks and financial institutions.
rules.non_resident_rules: Non-residents may open and operate foreign currency accounts and transfer funds freely without prior approval.
rules.business_invoicing_settlement: Business transactions may be invoiced and settled in euros or foreign currency. Cross-border payments and repatriation of funds are handled freely through authorised financial institutions.
rules.exchange_controls: France maintains no general exchange controls. The regime is fully liberalised for both current and capital account transactions within the Eurozone framework.
rules.banking_conversion_practicality: Foreign exchange conversion and transfers are widely available through banks, licensed money exchange houses, and ATMs throughout France.
